page.layout: One page of text, one column of running text in roman and italic with Greek inside it. No marginal notes. Printed page number 124 at the head. Catchword "exau-" at the right below the last line.

main_text.p: Imperatoribus ante assensum Pontificis Romani, licet invitum Photium in sedem restitutum fuisse, tum ab ipsis petitam a Pontifice restitutionem. Id non approbat, licet non videatur improbare. εἰ καὶ ἡ [?] [illegible, ~60 letters] Licet nostra pietas, vim Photio inferens substituerit illum ante nos, hoc est prius quam missi a nobis Legati istuc venirent. Malo tamen se, ne status Ecclesiae integer dissipetur, remedium dicit afferre ex indulgentia, qua severitas legum Ecclesiasticarum moderatur.

Non ergo probat restitutionem Photii, sed ausum illum Imperatorum, & vim illatam tolerat. Ubi enim necessitas fuerit, & vis, ibi ad utilitatem Ecclesiarum Dei, qui potestatem habet, dispensat. Si ante literas has Pontificis Photius receptus fuerat, & restitutus in sedem, frustra Pontifex tot inculcatis adhortationibus Photii reconciliationem Imperatoribus, aliisque Praesulibus suadet. Frustra enim quod actum est, fieri suadetur. Et qui a tot Synodis iustas ob causas, & ob ingentia scelera condemnatus, expulsus, inferisque per anathema devotus fuerat, & Christianorum nomine indignus declaratus, & ab Oecumenico Concilio

page.notes: The Greek sentence is faint and only its opening words are partly legible; the rest is marked illegible. The Latin is clear. Long s has been normalised to s and u/v, i/j to the vowel/consonant forms as instructed. The printed "Photij" was read as "Photii".
